children.counts: Simple 4-count steps forward followed by 8-count hand posturing.
children.game_version: The Mirror River game: two equal teams start on opposite sides of the room, walk slowly toward the center tape line to make one straight row, then freeze like statues while moving only their hands and heads.

seniors.counts: Counted in steady 4-count or 8-count phrase cycles matching recited chant lines.
seniors.seated_version: Perform the entire sequence seated upright on a chair, executing the supple hand movements and head tilts while omitting the marching entrance and kneeling transitions.
seniors.standing_version: Stand in place without traversing the stage, holding the erect torso posture and practicing the hand and head gestures with support nearby if needed.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Maintain a gentle, measured tempo with reduced range in wrist extension to avoid joint strain.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Supple, beautiful hand gestures (fola haka) that carry the primary artistic and narrative expression
movement_profile.footwork: Minimal lower-body involvement; occasional steps or lowering to a kneeling position
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Bilateral entrance from stage left and stage right, converging at the center into one or more parallel lines
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Stiff torso kept deliberately stationary; hip movement historically present but eliminated following Christian royal intervention
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Ground level; primarily standing with occasional kneeling, no jumps
movement_profile.posture: Stiff, conservative, upright body posture with suppressed hip and upper body swaying

signature_moves.description: Ensemble splits into wings and enters from left and right to merge into unified central lines
signature_moves.name: Fahaʻi entry

signature_moves.description: Supple, expressive posturing of the hands executed while keeping the torso stiff
signature_moves.name: Haka hand shaping

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Stately and restrained in modern execution; historically fast paced
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid exaggerated hip movement or loose upper-body swaying, which were explicitly banned by royal reforms in favor of conservative stiffness

music_profile.musical_form: Sequential poetic stanzas with recurring refrains (e.g., 'tulituli faiva, he tuli faiva ē')
music_profile.sound_description: The sonic texture is built on vocalized Tongan chants, featuring rhythmic vocal delivery, collective affirmation syllables, and recurring ancestral poetry sung by an accompanying choir or the dancers themselves.
music_profile.vocal_style: Poetic group chanting with call-and-response refrain lines

basic_steps: Divide the ensemble into two flanking groups offstage to the left and right
Process inward toward center stage until lines meet and merge into a single row
Assume an upright, stiff torso posture with minimal leg movement
Execute subtle, supple hand postures in coordination with head tilts while holding a seated, standing, or occasional kneeling posture
teaching.formation: Two or more flanking groups that enter from left and right and merge into one or more rows
teaching.level_notes: Beginners focus on the spatial convergence and holding torso stillness while coordinating wrist and hand postures with head inclinations.
teaching.rhythm: Chanted verse rhythm; metric counts not described in sources
